Diamond reports

Know what you are choosing.

A laboratory report helps describe a diamond. Read the actual document alongside the stone—not just a marketing badge.

IN THIS GUIDE
All education ↗
01

Begin with identity

Check the issuing laboratory, report number, date, and whether the stone is natural or laboratory-grown. Read disclosed treatments and comments. Use the laboratory’s own verification service rather than relying only on a seller’s screenshot or the phrase “certified diamond.”

02

Compare like with like

Review the measurements and weight, then the quality information provided by that report type. Natural diamond reports and laboratory-grown assessments do not all use identical terminology. GIA’s current D-to-Z laboratory-grown service uses a Quality Assessment with Premium or Standard categories; an older report or a different laboratory can have a different format.

03

Read beyond the headline

Ask which document belongs to the actual stone being sold and have its identifying features checked when needed. A report lookup confirms a record; it does not alone prove that the physical diamond in front of you matches it. Photographs and a viewing appointment can answer appearance questions that specifications cannot.

04

A report is not a price promise

A grading or assessment report is not an appraisal, insurance policy, resale guarantee, or guarantee of future value. GIA does not provide appraisals. If you need an insurance valuation, ask the insurer what documentation it requires and use a suitably qualified independent appraiser.
